walk-distance-displacement.alt: A person starts at x = −1 m on a number line marked from −2 m to +6 m, walks 5 m in the positive direction to x = +4 m, turns around and walks 2 m back to end at x = +2 m. Dashed curved arrows show the two legs of the walk. A solid arrow from −1 m to +2 m is the displacement, +3 m. The distance traveled is 5 m + 2 m = 7 m, a scalar; the displacement is +3 m, a vector pointing in the positive direction.
